stock.rule: Universe: S&P 100. Keep stocks above their 20-day average with a positive 5-day return. Rank by 5-day return, 20-day return, volume vs. 20-day average, and mentions in today's finance and AI headlines. Skip anything featured in the last 10 trading days. Mechanical, backward-looking, and not a recommendation.
stock.note: Hypothetical: buy at the open on the day featured, hold to the latest close, equal amounts, no fees or taxes. Five stocks over one week is mostly noise; judge the rule over months, not days.

stories.title: No one expected an American pope. Here's the inside story of how 'Bob' became Pope Leo
stories.excerpt: When the 2025 conclave began, no one expected an American pope. But by its end, Cardinal Robert Prevost had become Pope Leo. Here's a look behind the scenes.
stories.lead:
NPR's Daniel Burke and Scott Detrow covered the 2025 conclave that elected Pope Leo XIV. The following excerpt is adapted from their new biography of Pope Leo, American Pope, out Tuesday.

In the days immediately following Pope Francis' death, messages from friends poured into Cardinal Robert Prevost's phone.

Father Ramiro Castillo Castro, who had studied under Prevost in the 1990s, was among those who sent condolences. "Thank you, Ramiro," Prevost responded. "We have to pray a lot. Big hug."

stories.title: Flydubai co-pilot attacked captain with axe, UAE official says
stories.excerpt: The man accused of trying to take over the Israel-bound jet is named as Hamam al-Hammami by several media outlets.
stories.lead:
The co-pilot who attempted to take control of a Flydubai plane travelling to Israel attacked the pilot with a crash axe, the United Arab Emirates prosecutor general has said.

The flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv carrying more than 170 people plunged 17,000ft (5,200m) two and a half hours into its journey, before passengers managed to overpower the attacker and successfully take control of the plane.

Capt Smit Machchhar said he was lying on the floor injured when he realised the plane was sinking and he had to act, explaining: "I told myself to go for one last push to open the door from inside", which allowed the passengers in.

stories.title: Brazil's big political rematch: What to know
stories.excerpt: Four years after President Lula narrowly defeated Jair Bolsonaro, Brazil is back at the ballot box. This time, Lula faces Bolsonaro's son, Flávio, in a high-stakes rematch.
stories.lead:
RIO DE JANEIRO — Brazil's presidential election is a rematch of the country's bitter 2022 contest — but with a twist. President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva is facing Flávio Bolsonaro, the son of the man he narrowly defeated four years ago, Jair Bolsonaro.

Flávio, a 45-year-old senator, is carrying his father's political movement into Sunday's election. Jair Bolsonaro is now serving a 27-year sentence for plotting a coup to overturn that loss. His son has promised to pardon him if elected.

stories.title: The Supreme Court faces another term jam-packed with controversy
stories.excerpt: The Supreme Court term opens on Monday with big test cases on religion, guns and climate change. Plus, the emergency docket keeps popping.
stories.lead:
The U.S. Supreme Court formally opens a new term on Monday, with big test cases on religion, bans on semi-automatic weapons, climate change, immigration and — waiting in the wings — election law cases.

It used to be that the first Monday in October marked the beginning of a new Supreme Court term. And that's still true, technically. But for all practical purposes, the formerly quiet summer months after the court finishes its opinions in all argued cases no longer exists.

stories.title: Suppliers pile pressure on government over energy bills
stories.excerpt: Immediate action is needed to help households struggling with bills this winter, says trade body Energy UK.
stories.lead:
The government should take immediate action to help those struggling with energy bills this winter, the suppliers' trade body has said.

Energy UK said domestic gas prices, which rose on Thursday, and forecasts of steep rises in January meant inaction would lead to a longer-term, more costly and deeper crisis.

Figures revealed by the BBC earlier this week showed forecasters predicting a 16% rise in domestic energy prices in the new year for 20 million households on variable tariffs affected by regulator Ofgem's price cap.

stories.title: As Trump's proposed arch looms over D.C., protesters pin their hopes on the midterms
stories.excerpt: Democratic lawmakers, veterans and concerned citizens gathered in Memorial Circle to protest the arch Trump wants to build there. Their hopes lie primarily in a lawsuit and next month's midterms.
stories.lead:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Dozens of activists gathered at Memorial Circle in Washington, D.C., at rush hour Thursday to protest the 250-foot-tall arch that President Trump wants to build there.

Veterans, retirees and lawmakers spoke out — against its scale, its cost, its lack of Congressional approval, its gaudiness, its intrusion on nearby Arlington National Cemetery and more — next to a mockup made of tarp. The real arch, they said, would be 32 times taller.

stories.title: Tritons Win Two at Gary Troyer Tournament
stories.excerpt: The No. 9 UC San Diego men's water polo team fell to No. 6 Long Beach State, 17-16, after three overtime periods Sunday at the Mountain Pacific Sports Federation (MPSF) Invite.
stories.lead:
CLAREMONT, Calif. — The 12th-ranked UC San Diego men's water polo team won both of its games Friday at the Gary Troyer Tournament hosted by Pomona-Pitzer at Haldeman Pool.

In the early game, the Tritons took down Redlands by a score of 15-5. In the second and final game, UC San Diego earned a 16-10 victory against Pomona-Pitzer.

Redlands is ranked No. 2 nationally in NCAA Division III while Pomona-Pitzer is ranked No. 3 in NCAA Division III. Both teams play in the Southern California Intercollegiate Athletic Conference (SCIAC).
